description: Published card/ATM/POS data appears to be quarterly aggregates (counts of cards, acceptance devices, transactions). No public breakdown by scheme (Visa/Mastercard/Dina), by issuer bank, by contactless vs contact, or by merchant category was located.
The contents of the ZIP archives (sheet names, table inventory, series start dates, whether English column labels are present) were not inspected in this pass — only the parent pages were read.

The boundary between CBCG series and MONSTAT (Uprava za statistiku Crne Gore) series was not mapped, although the release calendar is jointly published and MONSTAT hosts the consolidated national calendar.

Coverage was conducted in Montenegrin/Serbian (ijekavian, Latin script) and English. Cyrillic-script variants of the key terms (Централна банка Црне Горе, статистика, платни промет) were not separately tested.

It is unclear how deep the CBCG online archives go for each dataset family and whether superseded vintages are retained after revision (the file links observed are current-period only for MFI and interest rates).
The quarterly payment services / e-money ZIP dataset — the source of card, POS, terminal-type and cash deposit/withdrawal series — has not had its actual file inventory inspected.

No archive of past monthly payment-traffic releases was located; the CBCG page appears to present the current month plus an annual aggregate. Historical monthly RTGS/DNS values may only be reconstructible from Bilten back-issues or press reports.
SEPA migration has no published national indicator. CBCG announces milestones but does not publish SCT/SCT Inst/SDD volume shares or the count of adhering Montenegrin PSPs.

Nearly all authoritative payment statistics for Montenegro originate from one publisher, CBCG, with no bank association, no domestic scheme, and no national statistics office series identified as an independent alternative.

MONSTAT (Statistical Office of Montenegro) and the Ministry of Finance were not directly scouted in this cell, although CBCG submits its release calendar to MONSTAT as part of the official statistics system.

NASO (Nacionalna organizacija za podršku pridruživanju / National Adherence Support Organisation) surfaced only via trade press; its own web presence and any publications were not located in this pass.

Bilingual coverage was achieved (Montenegrin/Serbian plus English) but no searching was done in Albanian, spoken by a significant minority, and none in Italian or Russian despite the tourism-driven card-acquiring market.
Three of the six outlets named in the coverage cell (Vijesti, Pobjeda, Dan) have only root-level or unverified URLs, with no confirmed economy-section or search endpoint.
Payment/card figures disclosed in TV and radio interviews (RTCG, Vijesti TV, Prva TV, PG TV) may never reach the text web; only the gradski.me item hinted at video-first reporting.
The cell was scouted at outlet level; individual economy/banking journalists who repeatedly break payment statistics were not identified.
Coastal and northern regional outlets and Albanian-language Montenegrin media were not searched; ATM availability and cash dependence are strongly regional (tourism coast vs north).
Media coverage is driven by bank PR (CKB, NLB, Erste, Lovcen, Hipotekarna, Prva banka). Their own newsroom/press pages, the origin of many quoted ATM/POS counts, were not enumerated in this cell.
Only one outlet (Aktuelno.me) exposed a browsable archive index; multi-year back-filling of payment coverage across the main outlets has no established path.

The EC Economic Reform Programme (ERP) / Economic Reform Agenda submissions for Montenegro and the Commission's joint assessments were not searched in this pass; they routinely carry financial-sector and payments-digitalisation measures with quantified targets.

IPA II/III programming documents and the EU Delegation's contract/tender records for financial-sector technical assistance in Montenegro were not enumerated; these identify contractors and deliverables for payments modernisation TA.

EIB Global and the Council of Europe Development Bank were not checked for Montenegro financial-sector/digital-infrastructure operations; also unchecked: World Bank Country Partnership Framework and Financial Sector Development programmes post-2020.

Local-language searching used Montenegrin/Serbian Latin script only; Cyrillic-script variants of key terms (платни промет, Црна Гора, инстант плаћања) were not tried and may surface additional regional/Serbian-language commentary and republished documents.
The EPC Register of Participants was identified but its bulk-export/filtering capability for country=ME (and whether historical snapshots are retrievable) was not tested in this pass.

Regional/IFI research producers that routinely cover Western Balkan payments (EBRD BEEPS merchant surveys, IMF Article IV and FSAP selected issues, EIB CESEE Bank Lending Survey, Vienna Initiative, wiiw) were not yet searched for their Montenegro cuts.
Scholar-level indexes (Google Scholar, Scopus, CrossRef, CONOR/COBISS.CG national bibliography) were not queried for Montenegrin-authored payment papers.

Montenegrin-Latin variants and transliteration alternatives (kartično poslovanje, POS terminali, bankomati, digitalizacija plaćanja, instant plaćanja) were only partly exercised; Cyrillic variants were not used at all.
No academic or consultancy source specifically analysing ATM/POS network economics or acceptance-network density in Montenegro was located.
UCG repository content has no discoverable unified search interface; thesis discovery depended on incidental search hits.
cejn.gov.me tender search could not be exercised (JS-rendered); its filter fields, CPV support, pagination and any JSON endpoint are unknown.

Career pages were confirmed for only one bank (Prva banka CG). The full set of licensed ME banks, payment institutions, e-money institutions and MFIs and their individual career/tender pages has not been enumerated.
LinkedIn job postings and company pages for ME banks/PSPs and for regional vendors selling into ME were not examined in this run (login-walled to search engines).

Municipal-level contracting authorities (opstine) and other SOEs (e.g. Montenegro Airlines successor, Zeljeznica, water/waste utilities, Uprava prihoda) were not individually enumerated as buyers of payment-acceptance and cash-handling services.

The State Commission for Control of Public Procurement Procedures (Komisija za kontrolu postupka javnih nabavki) publishes appeal decisions that reveal bidders and prices, but its own official site/URL was not located in this run - only a commercial aggregator claiming OCR access to that database.

Coverage used sr and en only. Montenegrin-language variants with the specific graphemes (s-with-caron, c-with-acute) were transliterated in queries, and Albanian-language channels (relevant in Ulcinj/Plav and for some employer ads) were not searched at all.
Contactless share and e-commerce (card-not-present) share of Montenegrin card transactions are not covered by any source located in this cell.
Card processors, ATM/POS vendors and independent ATM deployers operating in Montenegro were not identified in this pass; the cell covers regulator and issuer sources only.
Only the current-quarter (Q1 2026) file URLs were observed; the archive depth of the card/terminal ZIP series (the page's year archive reportedly reaches back toward 2006) was not enumerated.
Field definitions behind the card/terminal tables (active vs issued cards, ATM vs POS vs 'other device', double-counting of multi-scheme cards) are not documented in the statistics pages themselves.
All local searching was done in Montenegrin/Serbian Latin script; Cyrillic-script variants and Albanian-language sources (relevant to northern/eastern Montenegro media) were not searched.

The CBCG Annual Work Report and audited financial statements were identified as the likely carriers of cash-operations volumes (cash issued to / received from banks, unfit-note replacement counts, counterfeits withdrawn), but the individual PDFs were not opened and their tables not confirmed in this pass.

The quarterly ZIP bundle under 'Podaci o platnim uslugama i elektronskom novcu' was listed by table title only; the actual ATM-vs-POS breakdown granularity, the earliest available quarter, and whether values as well as counts are given were not inspected.

Cash-in-transit / cash-management companies, commercial cash-processing centres and retail cash-back schemes in Montenegro were not searched in this pass, and no local-language term set was exercised for them (e.g. 'transport novca', 'obezbjeđenje i prenos vrijednosti', 'CIT').

Customs Administration (Uprava carina Crne Gore) data on declared cross-border cash movements — a genuinely important physical-euro inflow channel for a euroised tourism economy — was inferred from the CBCG declaration rules but never searched directly.

Tourism seasonality is the dominant driver of Montenegrin cash demand but the tourism-arrivals and retail-turnover series that would let ATM withdrawal peaks be explained were only pointed at via the MONSTAT publications index, not enumerated.

All URLs in this slice come from search results and page navigation; several deep-link paths (regulation index, working-paper index, counterfeiting sub-page in Montenegrin) were constructed from observed site structure rather than fetched individually.

The Revenue and Customs Administration's own institutional pages (gov.me/upc) and its annual work reports were not directly fetched in this pass; the existence and contents of its publications section remain hypothesised from indirect evidence (a MONSTAT metadata entry referencing 'Pregled naplate prihoda Uprave carina').

EU-SILC / income-and-living-conditions statistics for Montenegro (material deprivation, ability to meet unexpected expenses, bank-account-adjacent deprivation items) were not located in this pass, though MONSTAT lists social-protection and living-standard domains.

Adjacent national fiscal/oversight bodies were not covered: Državna revizorska institucija (State Audit Institution), Uprava za katastar i državnu imovinu, and the Central Register of Business Entities (CRPS) — the last being the authoritative merchant-population register that complements MONSTAT's statistical business register.

It is unknown whether MONSTAT grants researcher access to anonymised microdata (Household Budget Survey, ICT survey) and under what terms, and whether data.gov.me exposes a working CKAN API for Montenegrin publishers.

All Montenegrin-language searching used Latin script only. Montenegro also uses Cyrillic officially, and some institutional pages (e.g. data.gov.me /cnr/ locale) render in Cyrillic, so Cyrillic-form queries were not exercised.

No supranational source found that publishes Montenegro card-scheme-level statistics (cards issued by scheme, transaction volumes/values, e-money) in a standardised cross-country form — the BIS Red Book, which would normally carry this, excludes ME.

Regional development banks and other supranationals that may compile ME banking/payments data — EBRD (Transition Report, Banking Environment and Performance Survey), EIB (CESEE Bank Lending Survey), Vienna Initiative, EFSE, OECD, UNCTAD — were not searched within this cell's budget.

No URL in this slice was fetch-verified; all entries rest on search-result evidence. Several specific dataset paths (IMF FSIC, IMF FAS path form, Data360 IMF_FAS, KNOMAD landing page) are plausible-but-unconfirmed.

Supranational sources give Montenegro only national-level annual figures; no sub-national (coastal vs northern municipalities) ATM/POS density is available internationally, despite FAS piloting rural/urban POS disaggregation.
Montenegrin/Serbian-language access points to supranational data (translated IMF country reports for ME, MONSTAT's Eurostat-facing pages, CBCG statistics in local language) were only lightly mapped.

Eurostat's Montenegro coverage is uneven: reporting indicates GDP and inflation available for 2025 while unemployment and net FDI series end around 2020, reflecting MONSTAT capacity constraints (operating at ~56% of planned staff).

Bankar magazine issues exist at least from no. 16 (2011) to no. 72 (2026) but no single archive index page was located; issue PDFs are scattered across wp-content/uploads by year/month with inconsistent filename conventions.

Association workshops (instant payments with Montran, EU payment regulation IPR/PSD3/FIDA) and the INFINTECH conference are documented, but no downloadable presentation decks with card/ATM/POS figures were found.
No association-published dataset aggregating member-bank card issuance, ATM/POS terminal counts or cash withdrawal volumes was identified.
The /en/ mirror exists but it is unclear whether all Serbian posts and PDFs are mirrored.
The EBF Montenegro Facts & Figures PDF (Dec 2024) and its 'previous editions' archive were referenced on the country page but the direct file URLs were not extracted in this pass.
Report hubs confirmed for CKB, NLB, Hipotekarna, Erste, Lovćen, Prva, Adriatic; not yet located for Ziraat Bank Montenegro, Universal Capital Bank and Zapad banka.
Bond and share prospectuses filed with the Capital Markets Commission (SCMN) were only sampled via one Prva banka PDF; the SCMN emitenti section was not systematically enumerated.
Foreign parents (OTP Group, NLB Group, Erste Group, Ziraat) publish Montenegro segment data in group annual reports; only the NLB Group page was captured here.
Only recent report years were surfaced (2021, 2023, 2024); no archive/back-series path was confirmed for any bank.
No source found that discloses mobile/e-banking user counts per Montenegrin bank; app-store proxies were used instead.
The CBCG page hosting financial reports of payment institutions and e-money institutions was not pinned to a confirmed URL.

Telco-operated payment and mobile-money propositions were not systematically scouted. MTEL was observed acting as a Western Union agent, and Crnogorski Telekom and One Montenegro recur in adjacent search results, but none was investigated as a payment actor.

Card acquiring and payment-gateway/PSP layer (e-commerce acquirers, card processors serving Montenegrin merchants) was not covered — this cell reached POS/ATM data only through the CBCG aggregate statistics, not through the processors themselves.

The CBCG register's annexed list 'Pružaoci usluga koji obavljaju aktivnosti koje se ne smatraju platnim uslugama' (providers of services not deemed payment services) was observed to exist but was not opened or enumerated.

Searches were run in Montenegrin/Serbian (Latin) and English only. Cyrillic-script variants and Albanian-language sources serving the Ulcinj/Plav populations — relevant for remittance corridors — were not queried.
No historical archive strategy was established for the registers, which are overwritten in place rather than versioned.

EU/EEA-passported payment institutions and e-money issuers serving Montenegrin residents were not scouted. Montenegro is not an EU member but joined SEPA in 2025, so foreign-licensed providers may serve the market without appearing in any CBCG register.

Several high-value endpoints in this cell were identified from search-result metadata and URL-pattern inference rather than direct fetch — specifically the Mastercard ME news index path, the Diebold Nixdorf newsroom path, and the Halcom ME country variant. None should be treated as confirmed live.

The processor/switch layer for Montenegro is not yet mapped. It is unknown which entity performs card processing and switching for most ME banks (candidates: Payten/ASEE processing, Bankart (SI), Multicard, in-house, or a Serbian processor), and no ME domestic card scheme or national switch was identified in this pass.

Several plausible vendor actors in this cell were not searched for lack of run time: NCR Atleos, Nautilus Hyosung, Ingenico, Verifone, PAX, Worldline/SIA, Nexi, Corvus Pay, Monri, Aircash, and local ME IT integrators (e.g. Čikom, Coming, Comtrade) that may front terminal or core-banking estates.
Bank-run ATM and POS locators for each Montenegrin bank were not enumerated. These are the most direct countable ATM/acceptance data available for ME and complement the MoneyGet IAD count.

Local-language searching was performed throughout in Serbian/Montenegrin Latin script only. Cyrillic-script variants ('Црна Гора', 'банкомати', 'платни промет') and Montenegrin-specific orthography (ś/ź forms) were not tried, and may surface additional or older announcements.
Only the currently indexed web was searched. MasterIndex has run since 2009 but only recent editions are reachable; earlier editions and delisted vendor announcements are not covered.
